- When sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.67 for multiple days) and news volume is high, model tends to overestimate prices — apply downward bias correction.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overshoots in subsequent periods — reduce forecast by 5–10% for the next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish sharply (e.g., -0.67+ change over 2–3 days), model underreacts — increase forecast by 3–7% to account for mean reversion.
- When news volume drops to 0 for 2+ days, model drifts toward historical mean — adjust forecast toward prior 7-day average.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes during sentiment volatility spikes — add 2–5% buffer if sentiment volatility > 0.5 in last 5 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true price movements by 1–3 days — shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is trending upward.
